prompt: I'm trying to figure out whether our new onboarding flow is actually improving 30-day retention. The numbers look better since we shipped it but I'm not sure how to be confident it's the flow doing it.
assertions: Claude explicitly names or describes the Rung 2 / interventional nature of the question — distinguishing 'the numbers look better' (Rung 1 correlation) from 'the flow caused the improvement' (Rung 2 causal effect)

Claude identifies at least one specific confounding mechanism with a direction — e.g., users who saw the new flow came from a different acquisition channel, cohort, or time period that would have improved retention anyway
Claude does NOT treat 'run a regression with controls for user characteristics' as a sufficient identification strategy for estimating this causal effect

Claude recommends a specific identification strategy — A/B test, holdout group, DiD using pre-period data, RDD at rollout date, or synthetic control — and explains why it addresses the identification problem
Claude does NOT treat the observed post-rollout improvement as evidence of causation without an explicit counterfactual or control group
